text:
infra-oncall: APAC GPU pool degraded ~35% capacity after node evictions. I triggered traffic shift to eu1 and started DNS failover, but we're still seeing a significant fraction of requests hitting APAC edges. Some resolvers returning old records.

maya: confirmed, ~20% of requests from our healthcheck cluster still resolve to apac-edge.redwood.ai. TTL on the A record was 3600s before the incident. Rolled TTL down to 60s at 21:02 UTC but traffic didn't shift fully. :thinking_face:

jin: can you paste a dig from an affected resolver? run `dig @8.8.8.8 apac-edge.redwood.ai A +short` and `dig apac-edge.redwood.ai @ns-cloud-1.redwood`

maya: here's a quick run from our eu probe:```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 apac-edge.redwood.ai A +short
35.182.12.7
```

samir: that looks like cached glue on some resolvers. Provider shows authority TTL change succeeded (3600 -> 60) at 21:02. A subset of public resolvers and enterprise CPEs are honoring the old TTL until their cache expires. Negative caching / DNSSEC validation not involved here.

lin: we also tried invalidating CDN routes and issuing a soft BGP withdraw for the APAC edge prefixes at 21:10, but clients that still resolve to the old IPs get TCP RSTs or long timeouts — connection fallback triggers are long on some SDKs.

ops-bot: ACTIONS TAKEN: lowered authority TTL to 60s; issued CDN invalidate; withdrew APAC edge BGP announcement (soft-withdraw); created fallback CNAME pointing to eu1-failover.redwood.ai. Incident ticket: INC-2026-042.

jin: two quick troubleshooting notes: 1) many corporate resolvers snoop and hold longer; lowering TTL mid-incident is best-effort. 2) If you change the CNAME target, some resolvers will cache the original CNAME chain — shorter TTLs on both the A and the CNAME help.

maya: sample dig showing CNAME chain state:```
; <<>> DiG 9.16 <<>> apac-edge.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
;; ANSWER SECTION:
apac-edge.redwood.ai. 3520 IN CNAME apac-edge-2026.redwood.net.
apac-edge-2026.redwood.net. 3520 IN A 35.182.12.7
```

samir: that ANSWER TTL of 3520 is why we saw tail traffic. We did the TTL change on the authoritative zone, but many resolvers returned cached entries with ~1h remaining. For affected customers we should: 1) advise them to flush DNS or restart resolver/clients if possible, 2) open a support ticket for large enterprise resolvers.

lin: pragmatic mitigation we used: 1) adjusted SDK retry policy to reduce long connection timeouts (lowered connect timeout from 30s -> 5s so SDKs fail fast and fallback to eu1), 2) temporarily spun up extra eu1 GPUs to absorb the increased load (~20 GPU cards, ~estimated cost $28/hr).

infra-oncall: note on costs — extra eu1 GPUs are pricey but cheaper than SLA breach. We'll log exact spend in the postmortem.

jin: a couple playbook updates to add from this incident: - pre-incident TTL downshift (staged: 3600 -> 300 -> 60 over 30m) for planned failovers - DNS pre-warm: create short-lived CNAME that points to failover target and prime major public resolvers where possible - include guidance for enterprise customers (support template to request cache flush)

maya: did anyone try authoritative zone serial bump + force re-announce with provider API? Some providers let you push a serial bump to encourage refresh. I kicked that at 21:12 and it returned success, but as noted that doesn't evict remote caches.

samir: edge note: avoid lowering TTL below 30s in normal times (dangerous for query spike/charge). For emergency playbook 60s is reasonable. Also add a checklist: verify both A and CNAME TTLs, check delegated NS TTLs, check DNS provider propagation dashboard.

ops-bot: SCHEDULED: postmortem meeting 2026-03-19 14:00 UTC, runbook update assigned to @maya and @jin.

lin: follow-up action that helped us: targeted customer comms to ~5 enterprise accounts with stuck resolvers asking them to restart resolver or add a temporary host override. That reduced error volume by ~12%.

infra-oncall: next steps summary: 1) update failover runbook with staged TTL downshift + provider API serial bump steps, 2) add pre-allocated standby GPU capacity in eu1 (on-call decision threshold), 3) craft support template for enterprise resolver flush, 4) retro and cost review tomorrow.

jin: logging note — add a metric for "requests served to deprecated-edge-ip" so we can detect stale-resolution tails faster in future.

maya: thanks all. I'll draft the runbook PR and paste the dig samples + timeline into the ticket.

infra-oncall: closing channel thread for now, will re-open if further anomalies. :white_check_mark:
